author: ohtadmin
title: Rental properties are not the problem
text:
To the editor:
As evidenced by an Oct. 23 letter in The Jamestown Press, there appears to be a recurring theme among some islanders that many of our problems are caused by short-term rentals.
Essentially, if only they were eliminated all would be good, e.g., our homes would be more affordable, our schools would have more students, and we won’t devolve into another Newport or Narragansett, etc.
My perspective comes from approximately 20 years as a rental specialist at Island Realty. I am informed by facts vs. rumor and speculation since I and my colleague produced the overwhelming majority of short-term leases during that time period.
Most landlords are Jamestowners who rent their residence to augment their income, often while traveling. The majority of tenants have school-age children, so our season is somewhat limited to the brief summer vacation calendar, while the rest tend to be older couples.
These are people who support our local businesses. Fortunately, unlike neighboring towns, our quiet island doesn’t attract the single, boisterous bar scene crowd.
Although there are a few pure investment homes, for most potential investors the cash flow cannot justify the cost of purchasing and ongoing expenses. In the more modestly priced Jamestown Shores area, with few exceptions, only waterfront/ water view homes are viable vacation rentals.
The reason property values continue to appreciate is not due to an increase in short-term rentals, (the inventory is relatively stable). It’s simply that our island has become increasingly desirable and prices are market driven. Unfortunately, that often excludes families with young children.
Dan Shapiro
Narragansett Avenue
